**Symptom (owner-reported, 2026-07-16 → WI-5125):** clicking **Chat** on a work item
spun on `loading chat…` **forever**. No error, no timeout, no console fault.

**Two independent bugs stacked**, which is why it looked like a hang rather than a
fault. Both are general traps; neither is chat-specific.

## Bug 1 — the literal DEFAULT makes a wrong write look like a right one

`agent_chats` (like `messages`, `executed_actions`, `agent_runs`,
`supervisor_notes`, `directive_summaries`, `feature_audit`) is a per-harness
**auto-updatable view** over a `harness_shared.*_consolidated` table. Every
consolidation migration ended with:

```sql
-- migration 116, and 118/119/120/170 in the same shape
ALTER VIEW <schema>.agent_chats ALTER COLUMN workspace_id SET DEFAULT 'default';
```

The comment above it read *"Column DEFAULTs so writers that omit these on INSERT
still pass through"*. `harness_slug` and `created_at` genuinely can be defaulted
that way — the view knows its own slug, and `now()` is always right.
**`workspace_id` cannot.** The active workspace is only known **in-process**
(the request's `x-papercusp-workspace` header → ALS, or the process pin — see
`activeWorkspaceId()`); a static literal in the DDL is a *guess*, and it is wrong
for every workspace except `default`.

So `createChat` omitted the column, the view filled `'default'`, and the INSERT
**returned success**. 181/181 rows were mis-tenanted. Meanwhile the UI reads
`agentChats.detail { id, workspaceId }` **scoped to the live workspace**, matched
zero rows, and could never see the row it had just created.

The contrast that proves it: `harness_features_consolidated` has **no** such view
default — its writers pass `workspace_id` explicitly — and its 1520 rows carry the
correct workspace. The literal default is not a convenience; it is the bug.

> **Rule.** A column whose correct value is only knowable at request time must be
> stamped **explicitly by the writer**. Defaulting it in DDL converts a loud
> `NOT NULL` violation into a silent wrong-tenant write. If you want a safety net,
> make the net *derive* the value — never assert a literal.

**This is now linted (WI-5243).** `findLiteralTenantDefault` in
`scripts/lint-migrations.mjs` fails any enforced-era migration that sets a literal
default on `workspace_id` / `hive_slug` / `tenant_id`, and the repo-wide scan runs
inside `lint-migrations.test.ts` — so `npm run test:affected` (which the
green-checkpoint gate runs) catches a reintroduction automatically. A *derived*
default (`current_setting(...)`) is legitimate and is not flagged. Note the lint
scans **raw** text, unlike its siblings: these `ALTER`s live inside a per-schema
`DO $$ … $$` loop that `stripSqlBodies` removes, so a stripped scan would pass —
that false green is the whole bug.

### Migrations are only half of it — the runtime scaffolder clones the trap

**Fixing the migrations is not enough, and this is the part that will bite you.**
`packages/operator-core/lib/scaffold-harness-schema.ts` builds these same views at
**runtime** for every NEW harness, and it carried five copies of the same literal
under a comment reading *"matches migration 116"*. So a migration that fixes every
existing schema still **decays one new harness at a time** — each newly created
harness is born with the bug. The migration lint scans `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/`
only, so it is structurally blind to that file; it has its own source-text guard in
`scaffold-harness-schema.test.ts`.

> **Rule.** When you fix schema DDL, grep for a **runtime** provisioner that emits
> the same DDL — `grep -rn "ALTER COLUMN <col> SET DEFAULT" --include=*.ts`. A
> migration fixes the past; the scaffolder decides the future. Fix both or the
> class comes back.

Editing that file has a sharp edge: its DDL lives inside a **JS template literal**,
so a **backtick** in a comment terminates the string and breaks the build with a
confusing `TS1005`. Apostrophes are fine; backticks are not.

### The net that already existed

`harness_shared.fill_workspace_id_from_projects()` — a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger that
derives `workspace_id` from the harness slug when it arrives NULL/empty — was already
attached to `work_items`, `harness_issues_consolidated` and `contributor_usage_events`.
The 7 later consolidations each hand-rolled a literal default instead of reusing it.
Migration **616** drops the literals and attaches that existing trigger to all 7.

**But the trigger is a net, not the fix.** It reads `harness_shared.projects`, which
on this box is a near-empty legacy registry (7 rows; it does not even contain
`papercusp`) — so for the reported case it resolves right back to `'default'`. Check
where a derive-trigger actually reads from before trusting it; an elegant-looking
trigger-only fix here would have been a **no-op that still looked correct**.

### Gotchas when changing these views

- **Ownership is not uniform.** ~240 harness schemas: most views are owned by
  `harness_admin` (the migration role), but `harness_org*`, `harness_papercup`,
  `harness_restart`, `harness_sheets*` are owned by `postgres_app`. `ALTER VIEW`
  requires ownership, so **one un-owned view aborts the whole migration** unless you
  wrap each `ALTER` in `EXCEPTION WHEN insufficient_privilege` and `RAISE NOTICE`.
- **Lock window.** `ALTER TABLE … DROP DEFAULT` needs ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, and a
  long-running `session_archive_files` COPY holds `AccessShareLock` on these tables
  for minutes. Use a **short** `lock_timeout` and retry — never queue an ACCESS
  EXCLUSIVE behind it, because every new reader then queues behind *you*.

## Bug 2 — `useSyncQuery` reports "no rows" as neither data nor error

This is what turned a data fault into an eternal spinner, and it applies to **every**
`useSyncQuery` consumer:

```ts
// zero rows resolves as:  { data: [], loading: false, error: null }
```

`ChatPanel.loadChat` set `chat` only when a row existed, and `loadError` only when
`error` was set. **Resolved-but-empty matched neither branch**, so `chat` stayed
null and `if (!chat) return <spinner/>` rendered forever. The panel had no bug in
its error path — it simply had no *empty* path.

> **Rule.** With `useSyncQuery`, `data: []` is a **real, terminal outcome**, not a
> loading state. Branch on all three: loading · error · resolved-and-empty. If a
> component renders a spinner whenever data is falsy, it will hang forever the first
> time a read legitimately returns nothing — and it will look like a network hang,
> sending you to the wrong layer entirely.
>
> Related: a **retry** button must `invalidate()` (refetch). Re-running a loader that
> reads the same cached rows re-derives the identical failure — a retry that cannot
> retry.

## How to tell these apart fast

The spinner points at the transport; the fault was in the data. Skip the layer
guessing and ask the DB who owns the rows:

```sql
-- Does the row exist, and under WHICH tenant?
SELECT workspace_id, count(*) FROM harness_shared.agent_chats_consolidated GROUP BY 1;

-- Compare against a table known to stamp correctly:
SELECT workspace_id, count(*) FROM harness_shared.harness_features_consolidated GROUP BY 1;
```

A table whose rows are **all** `'default'` while its siblings carry real workspaces is
this bug. Then replay the UI's exact read — it is the shortest path from symptom to
proof:

```bash
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:3070/api/zero-harness/rest-query?name=agentChats.detail\
&args=%7B%22id%22%3A%22<uuid>%22%2C%22workspaceId%22%3A%22papercusp-workspace%22%7D"
# rows: [] → the row is mis-tenanted (or absent). Not a transport problem.
```

`:3070` serves the **release** checkout, so it reflects DATA fixes immediately but
never your local code changes — verify code on `:3170` after
`dev:restart { target: 'staging' }`.

## Where the explicit stamp lives now

Every live writer into these per-harness views passes `activeWorkspaceId()`:

- `agent-chats-data.ts` — `createChat` (and `listChats` is workspace-scoped, which
  closes a second route to the same spinner: `openFeatureChat`'s
  reuse-before-create otherwise hands `ChatPanel` a foreign chat id).
- `execute-action.ts` — `messages` (×2), `executed_actions`, `supervisor_notes`,
  `directive_summaries`. The active workspace is correct for the *recipient's* row
  too: cross-workspace dispatch is unsupported in v1, so caller and recipient always
  share a workspace.
- `harness-agent-runs.ts` — already stamped explicitly; it was the model to copy.
- `feature_audit` — only `_retired` code writes it.

**Correct stamping does not break the readers.** These views filter on
`harness_slug` alone (no workspace predicate), so a correctly-stamped row is still
visible to every existing reader — verified before/after against
`messages_consolidated`, which carries fleet comms.

## ⚠ The converse trap: sometimes `'default'` is CORRECT, and "fixing" it is destructive

Everything above is about a literal `'default'` that is a **bug**. Read it together
with this section, or you will over-apply it. On 2026-07-27 a WI-684/P-007 audit set
out to migrate "the ~32 inline `?? 'default'` workspace fallbacks" and found, on
measurement, that **the string is overloaded with at least three legitimate meanings**
— and that "fixing" the highest-volume ones would have stranded live data.

`workspace_id = 'default'` currently means any of:

1. **A real, legacy workspace id.** `workspace-registry.ts` (see the `isKnownWorkspace`
   comment) notes the literal is "always treated as known — a defensive fallback for
   legacy pre-WI-5321 installs (whose real workspace really is id `default`)". On a
   legacy box it is an ordinary tenant sitting alongside the others.
2. **`DEFAULT_COORD_WORKSPACE`** — the coordination / p2p shared-partition **sentinel**
   (WI-1564). `events/await/store.ts` is explicit that the module takes *no* `workspaceId`
   input "full stop" (WI-3575): an earlier revision accepted one, and because the shell's
   identity carries `workspaceId: '*'`, awaits registered under a workspace the event key
   never matched and **the wake never fired**. `adv-roster.ts` documents the same mismatch
   from the read side — a workspace-scoped filter over `event_awaits` matched ZERO rows
   and silently rendered the /adv Blocked column empty.
3. **The session-transcript CORPUS namespace** — `search/session-ingest.ts` writes
   `session_turns` / `tool_usage_rollup` under the literal deliberately, commenting that it
   is "the session-transcript CORPUS namespace, which is not a tenant". Every reader filters
   `WHERE (workspace_id = $ws OR workspace_id = 'default')` (`agent-tools/search/sources.ts`,
   `agent-tools/sessions/search.ts`), so each tenant reads the shared corpus *in addition to*
   its own rows. Re-stamping those rows to a tenant would strand the corpus from everyone else.

> **Rule.** Before "fixing" a `'default'` workspace value, find the **reader**. If any reader
> matches it explicitly (`OR workspace_id = 'default'`), the value is a namespace or a
> sentinel and the write is correct. Only a value that no reader expects is a mis-scope.
> Bug 1 above is real precisely *because* its readers filter on the live workspace and
> therefore could never see the mis-tenanted row.

### Two measurement traps this audit hit

**Row count is not harm.** Ranking candidates by how many `'default'` rows they write puts
the *deliberate* namespaces on top — they are the highest-traffic tables in the system. In
the 7-day census, `session_turns` + `tool_usage_rollup` were 69% of all `'default'` writes
and both were correct by design. Rank by "does a reader expect this value", never by volume.

**A leak rate suspiciously close to 1/N usually means N, not a leak.** `system_health_ticks`
looked like a clean 5.5% partial leak (17,163 `'default'` rows against 292,250 scoped ones).
But the host had **18 registered workspaces**, and 1/18 = 5.6%: `'default'` was simply one of
them, health-ticked on the same cadence as every other (3,991 ticks in 2 days, against 3,992
for `scratch` and 3,985 for `lane9`). The writer threaded the workspace correctly all along.
When a leak rate lands near 1/N, check the population size before believing it is a bug.

### Why grep and the lint both miss this

A census built from the pattern `?? 'default'` inherits that pattern's blind spots. The
dominant sites in this audit were **hardcoded object literals** (`workspace_id: 'default'`),
invisible to that grep — and invisible to `lint:no-workspace-default` / `lint:scope-defaults`
too, since those scan SQL DDL rather than TypeScript values. The reliable move is to go to the
**data** (which rows actually get written, and which readers select them) rather than to a
code pattern.
